note: Binds GOAL_SPEC.md 9.1 outputs 5 through 9 for the four foundational proof families whose outputs 1 through 4 were measured PASS at issue #481. Outputs 1 through 4 are inherited and are NOT re-claimed here. This artifact records LOCAL_PASS or OPEN per family per output and claims no Q57/QG3 LIVE_PASS. Output 5 was OPEN for all four families at issue #482 because the maximum/adversarial fixture measured that the L1 envelope is EXHAUSTIBLE on the redeemer-carried route: every forced MPF branch level costs a measured 276 complete-signed-transaction bytes, and reaching the level that exhausts the 16,384-byte envelope is a fixed-target search of about 2^(4i) digests. That measurement stands: it is re-run here, its marginal cost is unchanged, and finding Q1X-F5 keeps it. What changed at issue #545 is that the route is no longer the only one. All four families were wired onto published-chunk carriage (midgard/fraud_proofs/chunked_inclusion_v1 delegating to the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator over midgard/mpf_chunked_proof_v1), whose step transaction is byte-identical at branch level 22 and at branch level 32 — the depth a 2^128 adversary reaches. The carriage dispatch this adds costs the redeemer-carried route a measured constant of about 700 script bytes, lowering ITS ceiling from branch level 21..23 to 19..20 (2^76 work at the cheapest family); that shift is recorded in adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote rather than hidden. Output 5 is re-decided per family: LOCAL_PASS where the chunked route is emulator-measured end to end AND no adversarial axis remains unexercised for that family (Q12, Q14); still OPEN for Q10 and Q11, whose second axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, is measured and does not fit at the admissible Cardano spend shape (finding Q1X-F6). Every measured number in this artifact was re-pinned at issue #606 from Vitest runner reports produced in the #606 tree: the #580 flat reversion and this ticket's own regeneration both moved step transaction sizes, and #580 ruling 2c deferred the re-pin to here because this artifact's verifier could not complete until the #608 pexcludes red was cleared.

adversarialDepthBound.measuredTitle: bounds the membership-depth axis with a measured marginal cost per level
adversarialDepthBound.construction: Two siblings are deterministically grinded per level so that the challenged transaction's hashed path branches at every nibble 0..N-1, each into a DISTINCT nibble slot. Distinct slots are what force a three-child node, which is what makes every on-path proof step serialize as MPF's largest `branch` shape rather than the cheaper `fork` or `leaf`. Candidate keys are a counter written into a fixed buffer, so the fixture is byte-for-byte reproducible.
adversarialDepthBound.cborVersusTransactionNote: The 139-byte figure is the MPF library's own compact CBOR cost per branch step, measured separately at levels 1 through 5 with exactly constant differences. The 276-byte figure is the cost in the COMPLETE SIGNED transaction, which is what the L1 envelope measures, and is roughly double because the proof reaches the chain as Plutus data in the step redeemer. Using the smaller number for envelope arithmetic would understate the exposure by a factor of two; both are pinned so that substitution cannot happen silently.
adversarialDepthBound.workModel: Forcing a branch at level i requires a transaction whose hashed path agrees with the challenged transaction's path on i chosen nibbles. That is a fixed-target search, not a birthday search, so it costs about 16^i = 2^(4i) candidate hashings, and the whole ladder is dominated by its last rung.
adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote: The per-level cost is unchanged at 276 complete-signed-transaction bytes and 139 MPF CBOR bytes, re-measured at #606; what has moved twice is the CONSTANT. At issue #545 every step that can open a trie took on the carriage dispatch that lets a prover choose published-chunk carriage, a measured ~700 bytes of spending script, which lowered this route's ceiling from branch level 21..23 to 19..20. At the #580 flat reversion and this ticket's regeneration the step transactions grew again — the field preimage now rides the step redeemer and every field-door-consuming step validator was recompiled — and the per-family ceilings fell to 15 (Q10), 17 (Q11), 19 (Q12) and 18 (Q14), each re-derived from the stage bytes measured in this tree. This bound block is measured on Q12, whose ceiling of 19 is the one unmoved by either shift. That is the price of the remediation, and it is paid on the route being remediated: the chunked route it buys has a marginal cost of zero bytes per level and is measured out to level 32 (chunkedProofCarriage). Keeping the walk itself in the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator rather than inlining it into every step is what holds the #545 shift to ~700 bytes; inlining measured ~3,700.

outputStatus.title: Maximum/adversarial proof-fit fixture
outputStatus.evidence: Four measurements exist, and all four are re-pinned at #606 from runner reports produced in this tree. Issue #482 added the first threshold-enforcing measurement of the complete correction path on the MINIMAL fixture; re-measured here its worst byte margins are Q10 2,978 at step-04, Q11 4,674 at step-04, Q12 5,365 at step-01 and Q14 3,838 at step-02. The #481 residual added the MAXIMUM/adversarial fixture: a deterministically grinded block forcing five all-branch levels into each family's step-01 membership proof, and for Q11 into the step-04 non-membership proof as well, with the marginal cost of one further level measured at two real depths (276 complete-signed-transaction bytes, 48,388.75 execution memory units, 14,976,664.75 execution steps) and the resulting per-family envelope ceilings at branch level 15, 17, 19 and 18. Issue #545 added the third: the same real prepare/submit pipeline with the proof carried by published chunks and verified by the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator, driven at branch level 22 — past every family's direct-route ceiling — end to end for all four families, whose worst carriage margins are Q14 3,359 at step-01, Q12 3,049 at step-01, Q10 2,978 at step-04 and Q11 2,790 at step-04, every stage inside the 20% execution reserve. Issue #549 added the fourth: the second adversarial axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, measured through the same pipeline for Q10 and Q11 — and at the admissible shape it does not fit.
outputStatus.whyOpen: Q12 and Q14 are LOCAL_PASS: their maximum is measured to FIT, because the depth an adversary can force no longer reaches the step transaction, and neither family carries the second adversarial axis at all (the invalid-range steps operate on the compact transaction and the zero-input family's challenged transaction spends nothing by construction). Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN, and no longer for want of a measurement: their chunked lifecycles are measured end to end at branch level 22 like their siblings', but the second axis IS measured and at the admissible shape it DOES NOT FIT. The admissible spend-input cardinality is 296 and the correction paths cross the 16,384-byte L1 envelope at 75 (Q10) and 196 (Q11); at 296 both proofs evaluate comfortably and miss on bytes alone. Finding Q1X-F6 records the numbers. Unlike the mechanism #549 published, this residual is byte-shaped and so is carriage-addressable in principle (§8's tier-2/tier-3 ladder, issue #612), but no such carriage is measured for either family, so nothing here settles the axis.
outputStatus.owner: Q12/Q14 closed at issue #545; Q10/Q11 chunked lifecycle and F6 measurement landed at issue #549, re-pinned at issue #606; the cells remain with issue #483 and the F6 residual with issue #612

residualFindings.finding: Output 5 is closed for Q12 and Q14 and remains OPEN for Q10 and Q11. The maximum/adversarial fixture that #482 recorded as missing exists and is runner-measured, and what it measures — that the redeemer-carried maximum does not fit (Q1X-F5) — is remediated by published-chunk carriage, now measured end to end for all four families (chunkedProofCarriage). Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN on the second axis alone (Q1X-F6), which does not apply to Q12 or Q14. That axis is measured, and at the admissible 296-input Cardano spend shape it does not fit — on bytes, not on execution.

Q10, Q11 and Q12 have no emulator valid-block negative, and Q14's is a step-advance negative rather than a full valid-block finalization negative. True valid-block emulator negatives exist for other families (input-no-idx and da-hash-preimage), so the pattern is available and the omission is a breadth gap, not a structural impossibility.
Q11's emulator journey does not assert slashingApproach, unlike Q10, Q12 and Q14. The removal still executes, but the correct-slashing half of 9.1 output 9 is asserted only indirectly for Q11.

The emulator runs at maxTxSize 65536 while proof fit is judged against the real 16384-byte L1 limit through l1ByteMargin. The two are deliberately different: the relaxed emulator ceiling lets a would-be-oversize transaction be built and then measured rather than failing opaquely during construction. Any future change to EMULATOR_PROTOCOL_PARAMETERS.maxTxSize must not be mistaken for a change in the pass criterion.

REMEDIATED BY CARRIAGE, measurement retained and re-pinned at #606. The 16,384-byte L1 envelope on the REDEEMER-CARRIED route is exhaustible by a block producer willing to grind: each forced MPF branch level costs a measured 276 bytes of complete signed transaction (139 bytes of MPF CBOR, roughly doubled by the Plutus-data expansion in the step redeemer), so that route runs out at branch level 15 (Q10), 17 (Q11), 19 (Q12) and 18 (Q14). Forcing level i is a fixed-target search costing about 2^(4i) candidate hashings, so the cheapest of the four is exhaustible at roughly 2^60 work — well inside the 2^128 reference adversary, which reaches level 32. Byte fit is the binding envelope: the execution-memory ceiling is 214 levels and the execution-step ceiling 515, both measured. All of that remains true and is still asserted executably by the maximum fixture, which fails if any ceiling moves. Those ceilings are lower than the 21..23 issue #482 published and lower again than the 19..20 issue #545 published; the per-level cost is unchanged through both moves, only the constant moved — first by the carriage dispatch every trie-opening step now carries, then by the flat reversion and this ticket's regeneration — and adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote records why. A second consequence of the flat reversion is recorded per family rather than hidden: for Q10 and Q14 the largest stage of the correction path is now a step the depth axis does not reach at all, so their whole-fixture worst margins are identical in the minimal and maximum fixtures and the derived ceiling above is the conservative reading; the stage the axis does reach, step-01, is measurably tighter in the maximum fixture for all four families. What has changed in substance is that the direct route is no longer the ONLY route: issue #545 wired all four families onto published-chunk carriage, whose step transaction is byte-identical at branch level 22 and at branch level 32 (chunkedProofCarriage.depthInvariance), so the griefing vector no longer censors the correction path. The finding stays recorded rather than deleted because the direct route still ships and a prover who chooses it still faces this ceiling.

residualFindings.finding: MEASURED; THE EXECUTION WALL IS GONE AND A BYTE-CARRIAGE GAP REMAINS. The second adversarial axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, is exercised end to end for Q10 and Q11, and its verdict is re-pinned here from a runner report for the first time since #580 inverted it — #580 ruling 2c deliberately left this body un-re-pinned, because this artifact's verifier could not complete until #606 cleared the #608 pexcludes red. The admissible cardinality is unchanged at 296, the smallest of the consensus profile's 16,384-item guardrail, its 32,768-byte spend-inputs preimage field bound (862 inputs at 38 bytes each), and the Cardano script-spend shape already pinned as maximum_cardano_spend_redeemer_count. What is retracted is the mechanism. The counted-era claim — execution memory binding at ~276,000 units per input from re-hashing an authenticated bounded collection, with Q10 fitting 39 inputs and Q11 40, and neither proof evaluable at all at 296 — is measured false in every part. Under the flat commitment there is no collection to reproduce: step memory moves by 8,036 units over Q10's further 222 inputs and 3,212 over Q11's further 101, about 36 and 32 units per input, and at 296 both journeys build and evaluate at 625,256 and 495,554 memory units, better than seventeen times inside the 11,200,000 reserve ceiling. The binding envelope is L1 transaction bytes, at a measured 41 (Q10) and 42 (Q11) complete-signed bytes per input on the binding step: Q10's step-04 fits at 74 inputs with 6 bytes of margin and crosses the envelope at 75 (-35), Q11's step-02 fits at 195 with 39 bytes and crosses at 196 (-3). The exposure that survives is real but different in kind, and smaller: with the legacy builders' unconditional tier-1 inline carriage, a challenged transaction spending more than 74 (Q10) or 195 (Q11) admissible inputs still cannot be corrected, and that still costs the adversary nothing to arrange. Unlike an on-chain execution wall it is remediable by moving bytes — §8's tier-2/tier-3 ladder, off-chain only, no validator touched — but no such carriage is measured for either family here, so the cells stay OPEN and the finding stays a defect rather than an observation. Issue #612 owns the builder-side fix over the bands (74, 296] and (195, 296].

chunkedProofCarriage.mechanism: The MPF proof is published beforehand across bounded UTxOs whose inline datum carries nothing but canonical mpf.ProofStep values (mpf_chunked_proof_v1.ProofChunkDatum, at most 16 steps and 2,304 bytes each). The step transaction references them and names their order as indices into tx.reference_inputs; midgard/fraud_proofs/chunked_inclusion_v1 concatenates the chunks and verifies the complete proof atomically against the very root the challenged header commits. The redeemer-carried route is retained unchanged — it is cheaper for every proof that fits — so the carriage is a prover-chosen sum type (NativeTxInclusionCarriage / NonMembershipCarriage), not a replacement.

onchainSeam.whyMerkelized: Compiling the proof walk into every step that can open a trie added a measured ~3,700 bytes to each step's spending script, which the step transaction carries on EITHER route — taking the redeemer-carried route's ceiling from branch level 21..23 down to 8..9. Remediating one route by degrading the other is not a remediation, so the walk lives in one merkelized withdraw validator shared by every family, exactly as phas.ak and pexcludes.ak already host the single-transaction walks. The residual cost to the direct route is the carriage dispatch alone: ~700 bytes, two to three forced levels.

depthInvariance.note: Ten further forced branch levels. On the redeemer-carried route those levels cost 10 * 276 = 2,760 more complete-signed-transaction bytes, which is what exhausts the envelope. Here the step transaction is byte-identical, because it carries one small integer and one reference input per CHUNK rather than per level. The proof itself did grow (3,060 to 4,450 CBOR bytes); only its carriage did not. The depth a 2^128 adversary reaches (32) is therefore no longer a censorship lever on the step transaction.

chunkedProofCarriage.depthConstruction: The depth is synthesised rather than grinded, and deliberately so: a genuinely grinded level-22 trie costs about 2^88 digests, which is the adversary's cost and the whole point of finding Q1X-F5, not something a fixture can pay. The proof is a real MPF proof of a real trie shape (an all-branch ladder, MPF's widest step), verified by the library's own verify, and the challenged header is then made to commit exactly the root that proof proves — so the step's counted-root authentication is genuine. The grinded fixture in submit-init-emulator-max-proof-fit.test.ts remains the source of the COST bound; this one measures carriage. See demo/midgard-fault-proofs/tests/support/synthetic-deep-proof-v1.ts.
chunkedProofCarriage.sharedRootOpenings: Q12 and Q14 open the challenged block's transactions trie exactly once, so issue #545 could give each a standalone synthetic ladder. Q10 and Q11 cannot: double-spend opens the SAME root twice for membership (tx1 at step-01, tx2 at step-02) and no-input opens it once for membership and once for ABSENCE (the phantom input's producing transaction, at step-04), and every step re-authenticates its opening against the one root the challenged header commits. Two independent ladders each determine their own root, so the fixture builds what a real trie would hold instead: one shared branch node whose child slots carry the sub-tries of the individual ladders, with every opening's top-level neighbours read out of that same node. The library's own Proof.verify is what confirms each opening reconstructs the one root. See syntheticDeepSharedRootProofsV1 in demo/midgard-fault-proofs/tests/support/synthetic-deep-proof-v1.ts.
chunkedProofCarriage.secondPublicationNote: Q10 and Q11 publish twice, because each opens the trie twice and a publication carries one proof. The second publication is submitted immediately before the step that consumes it, which is also what keeps its UTxOs out of every earlier transaction's fee selection. Both publications survive the steps that reference them, which the suite asserts.

They drift in the last digits run to run because the emulator-derived validity interval moves, so the threshold assertion is the binding claim, not these constants.

spendInputCardinalityBound.derivationTitle: derives the admissible spend-input cardinality from the consensus profile
spendInputCardinalityBound.admissibilityDerivation: Three protocol constraints bound how many inputs an admissible challenged transaction may spend, and the smallest is the one a fraud proof must survive. (1) MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.maxSpendInputCount = 16,384, which is bounded_collection_v1.max_tx_size_derived_item_count in onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/bounded-collection-v1.ak; its own source calls it a one-byte-per-item encoding floor that can never reject a shape Cardano could fit, so it is a guardrail, not the effective bound. (2) MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.maxSpendInputsPreimageBytes = 32,768, twice the preserved L1 envelope, in demo/midgard-core/src/consensus-profile-v1.ts; at 38 bytes per canonical TransactionInput item it admits 862. (3) The Cardano script-spend shape boundary this repository already pins: 296 inputs each carrying a spend redeemer, maximum_cardano_spend_redeemer_count in onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx.max-redeemers.test.ak, which validators/fraud-proofs/input-no-idx/step-02.ak already names as the shape a Q13 proof must handle. 296 is the smallest, and is the admissible cardinality these two families are measured against.
spendInputCardinalityBound.ceilingNote: Both the execution ceilings and the byte envelope are named, because the axis changed which one it binds on. Execution is judged against Cardano's own 14,000,000-unit transaction memory cap and 10,000,000,000-unit step cap, which is what EMULATOR_PROTOCOL_PARAMETERS carries and what every other execution measurement in this artifact is judged by; the memory cap is BELOW the consensus profile's 16,500,000-unit capability floor, so it is the conservative reading. Under the counted commitment the 20%-reserve memory ceiling of 11,200,000 was what this axis ran into. Under the flat commitment it is not close: the measured step memory at the admissible 296-input shape is 625,256 (Q10) and 495,554 (Q11), between seventeen and twenty-two times inside that same reserve ceiling. What binds is the 16,384-byte L1 envelope on the step transaction that carries the preimage in its redeemer.
spendInputCardinalityBound.expectationCorrected: Two expectations are now measured false, and they failed in opposite directions. Issue #482 expected this axis to bind on the spend-inputs WITNESS PUBLICATION transaction; issue #549 measured that it did not, and the flat reversion then retired the publication entirely — both families now carry the field preimage in the step redeemer (§8.3 tier 1), the double-spend journey's step-03 and step-04 captures hold exactly one submission each where they used to hold two, and no witness-publication stage exists to measure. Issue #549's own finding then expected execution memory to bind, at ~276,000 memory units per input from re-hashing an authenticated bounded collection; that mechanism does not exist under a flat commitment, which authenticates the whole field preimage once against its flat hash and reaches an item by arithmetic offset and slice. Measured across the whole admissible band the step memory moves by 8,036 units over 222 further inputs (Q10) and 3,212 over 101 (Q11) — about 36 and 32 units per input against a counted-era 276,000, four orders of magnitude down. The binding envelope is L1 transaction bytes, at a measured 41 (Q10) and 42 (Q11) complete-signed bytes per input on the binding step.
spendInputCardinalityBound.rePinProvenance: Issue #580's close comment (2026-08-15, ruling 2c) left this block's body fields deliberately un-re-pinned: the flat reversion had already inverted the finding, but this artifact's verifier could not complete while the #608 pexcludes empty-sentinel red stood, and an unverifiable pin is the gate-that-cannot-fail hazard. #606 removes that red (the ledger_trie-style empty-sentinel translation ahead of mpf.from_root), so the verifier reaches this block for the first time and every number below is taken from a Vitest run of the cited suite in this tree rather than from the superseded artifact or from any review text.
spendInputCardinalityBound.admissibleShapeTitle: reaches the admissible Cardano spend shape on execution and misses it on bytes alone
spendInputCardinalityBound.whyNotRemediatedHere: The exposure is byte-shaped, so unlike the retired execution wall it CAN be moved off the step — that is the whole difference from the finding this block used to publish. §8's carriage ladder exists for it: above tier 1 the same preimage publishes once as a raw UTxO (tier 2) or as certified chunks (tier 3) and is reached by reference for a handful of index bytes, with no validator change. It is recorded as NOT remediated because no such remediation is measured: the legacy no-input and double-spend step builders these journeys drive carry the preimage inline unconditionally, so nothing here drives either family at 296 on a higher tier, and a remediation claim without a measured end-to-end block would be exactly the unfalsifiable prose this gate exists to refuse. Issue #612 owns the builder-side tier selection; its acceptance baseline is the band left open at tier-1 carriage, (195, 296] for Q11 and (74, 296] for Q10 — one input wider at each lower edge than the (196, 296] and (75, 296] #580 recorded, because this ticket's regeneration grew every field-door-consuming step validator.
